newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Consortium sets $1.5 bln Mercosur gas duct plan.
newsitem.headline: Consortium sets $1.5 bln Mercosur gas duct plan.

text.p: A consortium including Japan's Marubeni Corp and Mobil Corp of the United States announced Wednesday it intends to build a $1.5 billion gas pipeline running from Argentina to Brazil.
The group said in a statement it intends to construct a 1,900 mile (3,100 km) pipeline from Salta in north western Argentina to Sao Paulo in Brazil, supplying potentially 70 million people with gas.
The other partners in the group are Alberta Energy Co Ltd of Canada and Petrolera Argentina San Jorge.
It is estimated the pipeline would carry up to 25 million cubic metres of gas daily. Construction is expected to be completed between 2000 and 2001.
The project is being developed together with regional energy authorities in Argentina and Brazil.

A spokeswoman from Petrolera San Jorge said the project will be officially presented March 25 and called "Mercosur Gas Pipeline," after the customs union formed by Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.
This is the latest in a string of large gas projects that have been announced to link up Latin America's southern cone recently.
Lucio Noto, chairman and chief executive of Mobil, visited Argentina in November when he had a meeting with President Carlos Menem.
After the meeting he said Argentina would play a key part in a "regional gas strategy" for the oil company.
